SMTO-FIL-0014 — SMTO couldn't find the text it meant to change

GUID: 39595bb0-2bc5-4770-8f3b-248fd3976f2f
Slug: file-match-not-found
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO tried to edit a file, but the exact text it wanted to replace isn't in the file as it is now. The file wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to read the file again before making the change. The file may have changed since SMTO last looked, so it needs the current text to aim at.
  2. If you or someone else edited the file in the meantime, tell SMTO what changed, and close other programs that are editing it. Edits made elsewhere can remove or reword the exact text SMTO planned to replace.
  3. If you gave SMTO the text to replace, copy it again straight from the file and paste it into your message. Small differences such as an extra space or curly versus straight quotes prevent an exact match.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the edit as done and the file shows the new text in the right place.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to rewrite the whole file to get around this; that could undo changes someone else made.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file.edit was rejected because an edit's exact old_text anchor occurs zero times in the file's current content; nothing was written.

What this means

  • The literal old_text requested by an edit occurs zero times in the current loaded text. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The literal old_text requested by an edit occurs zero times in the current loaded text.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the current relevant text and compare exact characters and newline handling with old_text.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the target with file.read and rebuild the edit using an old_text anchor copied verbatim from current content, including whitespace and line endings, and pass the fresh revision as expected_revision (gateway_core/file_mutate.edit).
  • Read the current file and construct the edit against its actual content.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended exact match is present in the current reviewed revision.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.
